entries.title: Redridge Mountains
body: Red stone hills and pine forest east of Elwynn, gathered around the blue water of Lake Everstill. The mountains fall under the sovereign right of the King of Stormwind, and the township of Lakeshire, on the lake's northern shore, is their heart.

These days Lakeshire is under siege. Orcs of the Blackrock clan have come down from the Burning Steppes and taken Stonewatch Keep, gnolls of the Redridge and Shadowhide packs prowl the hills, and murlocs fish out the lake. Reinforcements promised from Stormwind have never arrived, and the guards on the bridge spend their watches asking each other when they will.
sources: quest 128 description (sovereign right of the King of Stormwind)

entries.title: Lakeshire
body: A township of timber houses on the northern shore of Lake Everstill, governed from its town hall by Magistrate Solomon and defended by Marshal Marris and a handful of Stormwind guards. During the last orc uprising Chef Breanna fed the whole brigade of Stormwind troops, and the town's iron was melted down for bullets, swords and armour.

Now its people are penned in like cattle. Supplies come late or not at all: the bridge from Goldshire was blown out, a boat carrying replacement tools was sunk by an orc catapult, and the barkeep's shelves are running dry. Life goes on regardless. The waitress Darcy sends lunch out to Guard Parker on patrol, and the herbalist Martie Jainrose keeps a garden of daffodils that a boar keeps trampling.

entries.title: The Everstill Bridge
body: The bridge that carries the road from Elwynn across the mouth of Lake Everstill into Lakeshire. When it was blown out, Lakeshire lost its easiest road to the rest of the kingdom.

Foreman Oslow has his crew working to rebuild it, but the materials keep disappearing. A caravan of iron sent from Stormwind was hijacked by gnolls and dragged into the hills behind the town, and Oslow can be heard urging his men on regardless: the bridge has to be rebuilt.
sources: creature 341 line (we've got to get this bridge rebuilt)

entries.title: Lake Everstill
body: The long lake at the centre of Redridge, famous for its spotted sunfish. Dockmaster Baren buys every one he can get, and the children of Lakeshire fish from its shore, though their parents tell them not to swim because of the mean things underwater.

Lately large groups of murlocs have dropped anchor along its shores and are fishing up a storm. The dockmaster finds it strange to see them so far from the sea, and wonders whether they came inland running from something.

entries.title: Stonewatch Keep
body: The fortress that once guarded Redridge's northern pass to the Burning Steppes. Blackrock orcs who crossed from the Steppes took it in a bloody battle, and from its walls they raid every farm north of Lakeshire.

Their warlord Gath'Ilzogg holds the keep and plans the clan's further attacks from inside it. Shadowcasters among the orcs carry midnight orbs, demon-tainted devices that have struck down many of Redridge's defenders. Lakeshire calls the warlord's death the first step in taking the keep back for the kingdom.

entries.title: Stonewatch Tower
body: The one watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep still standing intact. From its top a watcher can see across the whole keep.

The mage Theocritus had a Glyph of Azora hidden up there in a chest or a jar, where the orcs would not notice it, so that he could look into the minds of the Blackrock inside. What he learned was that the orcs were fighting a war of their own against the warlock Morganth.

entries.title: Render's Valley
body: A scorched valley in the south-east of Redridge, under the mountains that divide it from the Burning Steppes. The Blackrock orcs camp here as well as at Stonewatch, and the marshal wants any orc found in this south-eastern pocket hunted down.
The orcs are not the only danger. Black dragon whelps fly about south of Lakeshire and like to wander, and the stablemaster Verner Osgood pays his debts in the scales of their underbellies.
sources: quest 20 description (more in the southeastern pocket of Redridge)

entries.title: The Blackrock Encampment
body: A Blackrock camp north of Lakeshire, just west of the road to the Burning Steppes, where the champions who lead each unit of the clan gather.

After the battle at Stonewatch Keep, Corporal Keeshan of the 12th Sabre Regiment was dragged away by the orcs and held prisoner in a cave here. Most of his regiment had been killed. Notices in Lakeshire promised a reward to anyone who brought him home, and Keeshan, limping and badly hurt, eventually reported for duty again to Marshal Marris.

entries.title: Tower of Ilgalar
body: A lone tower in the eastern foothills of Redridge, guarded by a stone lion. It is the home of the warlock Morganth.

From here Morganth spreads terror and misery through the region. He commands the Shadowhide gnolls who camp around the tower, and he fights a war of his own with the orcs of Stonewatch Keep. His rival Theocritus, the High Mage of Tower Azora, keeps watch on the place through a glyph set on the lion statue.

entries.title: Rethban Caverns
body: Caves north of Lakeshire, named after Bart Rethban, the man who first found ore in them. Rethban ore is weaker than iron once smelted, but its dark, flat colour makes it valued by scribes for their dyes, and the Northshire library uses it to copy its books.

Lakeshire usually keeps some in stock. Not now: Redridge gnolls have moved into the caverns, their drudgers are digging out the ore for themselves, and the town is too busy preparing for the orcs to take it back.

entries.title: Alther's Mill
body: A sawmill and farmland in the hills north of the lake. Verner Osgood keeps his stable on this side of town, outfitting horses for the Stormwind guard.

The ridge above the mill is gnoll country. Brutes and mystics prowl there, taking the horses when they stray, and above the rest of the baying, the hunters of Lakeshire can pick out one louder cry: Yowler, the pack's leader.

entries.title: Three Corners
body: The meeting of roads in the south-west of Redridge, where the highway from Lakeshire turns towards Elwynn and the road to Duskwood runs off south. Guard Parker patrols the stretch towards Darkshire, with a packed lunch from Darcy when someone can bring it.

From the road, Parker has seen gnoll encampments gathering to the north and east. Gnolls that close to Elwynn may be poised to push into the kingdom's heartland, and Lakeshire, already outnumbered, is ill equipped to stop them.

entries.title: Magistrate Solomon
body: The judge who governs Lakeshire. When the siege began he sent to Stormwind for help, and was told reinforcements would come as soon as the King gave word. They never came.

Solomon did not wait. He wrote to Gryan Stoutmantle of the People's Militia in Westfall and to Lord Ebonlocke of Darkshire, and learned that both had been abandoned by Stormwind too. That the army had pulled back from three provinces at once convinced him there was treachery somewhere in the kingdom, and he means to get to the bottom of it.

entries.title: Marshal Marris
body: The commander of Lakeshire's defence, and the man who named the boar Bellygrub. With too few soldiers, he leans on anyone willing to fight the orcs in his place.

Marris wants the Blackrock thinned out wherever they are found, their shadowcasters' midnight orbs destroyed, and the head of Tharil'zun, the crafty orc who leads the outrunners ambushing the road between Lakeshire and Stonewatch.
sources: quest 34 description (Marshal Marris has taken to calling Bellygrub)

entries.title: Gath'Ilzogg
body: Warlord of the Blackrock clan in Redridge, and the orc who led the attack on Stonewatch Keep and the raids against Lakeshire. Wanted posters call him extremely dangerous.

His executioner, Targorr the Dread, tortured captured soldiers on a whim. Targorr was later taken and sentenced to die in the Stormwind Stockade, but a noble put a hold on the execution, and the guards of Lakeshire suspect foul play.

entries.title: Morganth
body: A warlock of great power living in the Tower of Ilgalar, declared an enemy of Stormwind by the court of Lakeshire. He controls the Shadowhide gnolls through pendants they wear, and under the law of the township, any gnoll who aids him is condemned to death.

His rival Theocritus spent months learning to listen through those pendants. He discovered that Morganth was searching for the Scythe of Elune, and may already have found it. With it, the warlock's dark might would have been felt across Redridge and the whole kingdom.

entries.title: The Blackrock in Redridge
body: The Blackrock clan have been in Blackrock Mountain since the Second War, and in the years since the last orc uprising they have pushed out of the Burning Steppes again. In Redridge they took Stonewatch Keep, killed most of the regiment defending it, and dragged the survivors off as prisoners.

The kingdom has been slow to answer. Lakeshire's guards still wait for the 2nd Battalion from Stormwind, and everyone in town has a theory why it has not come. Until it does, the township is held by its own few guards and whoever wanders through willing to fight.
sources: pre-Cataclysm lore: Blackrock Mountain after the Second War

entries.title: Something Amiss in Stormwind
body: Lakeshire's letters went out to Stormwind, Westfall and Darkshire, and every answer told the same story. Westfall's People's Militia was formed because Stormwind deserted it. Darkshire's Night Watch was formed because the guard left when foul magic seeped into Duskwood. Stormwind's own general promised reinforcements that never marched.

Magistrate Solomon came to believe it was the beginning of a conflict, not the end of one. Somewhere in the capital, someone is keeping the kingdom's army from its own people, and while that goes on, Lakeshire must defend itself.
sources: quest 386 description (a noble put a hold on the execution)
